title: Adaptive scenario sampler and profile validator for model onboarding
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Goal: Improve the benchmark harness used during model onboarding so that published performance profiles are representative and robust across realistic input distributions. Deliver two cooperating components: (1) an adaptive scenario sampler that synthesizes and prioritizes dataset+prompt permutations driven by live telemetry and curated failure cases, and (2) a profile validator that runs a meta-eval suite to ensure a generated profile meets invariants before it is published to the model catalog and used for version pinning.

Scope and deliverables:
- Adaptive scenario sampler: rules engine + sampling scheduler that can consume (a) customer telemetry histograms (token length, prompt templates, common prefixes), (b) curated adversarial prompt buckets, and (c) synthetic perturbations (typos, truncated context, long-prefix). The sampler should output deterministic sample sets for reproducibility and a randomized mode for stress testing.
- Profile validator: a lightweight meta-evaluator that asserts performance invariants (p50/p95 latency ceilings, token-cost delta thresholds vs baseline, top-k exact-match for small-qa, hallucination-rate upper bounds on selected evals). If a profile fails validation, it is marked Draft and a regression report is generated.
- Integration work: hook sampler+validator into the onboarding pipeline so model owners can opt into "strict" or "fast" profile publishing flows. Add UI flags for rollout (Console changes tracked separately).

Acceptance criteria:
1) For three onboarding models in the staging catalog we can produce a reproducible profile that includes: latency distribution, cost estimate, and qualitative eval scores. These profiles must pass the validator in at least the "fast" mode.
2) Validator produces actionable report (failing evals, example inputs, traces, suggested mitigations) within 15 minutes for a model sampled to 1k examples on our k8s test fleet.
3) Sampler supports input from a telemetry export (CSV or JSON histogram) and a local curated bucket; sampling config documented in Confluence.

Design decisions and trade-offs considered:
- Determinism vs coverage: we chose a default reproducible seed + an optional randomized sweep. Deterministic sets are required for releases and pinning; randomized sweeps are for stress/regression hunting.
- In-harness telemetry vs external signals: to keep onboarding fast we only ingest aggregated histograms exported from telemetry (no PII) rather than live streaming requests. This reduces freshness but simplifies compliance.
- Validator strictness modes: "fast" (coarse invariants, 1k samples), "strict" (detailed checks, 10k samples). Fast mode targets onboarding speed; strict mode used for Dedicated/Private customers.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Spike (1 week): prototype sampler that reads histogram CSV and outputs deterministic sample set. Prototype validator that runs a canned eval runner. (Done; spike PR linked).
- Iteration (2 weeks): add perturbation generators, integrate adversarial buckets, implement validator reporting.
- Integration & docs (1 week): wire into onboarding flow, add Confluence doc, add Console toggle for profile strictness.

Metrics to track:
- Profile pass-rate by mode (fast/strict)
- Time-to-validate (median)
- False-positive rate where validator flags a profile but downstream canary passes
- Number of onboarding rollbacks triggered by profile regression detection

Artifacts and links:
- Spike notes and design: Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Adaptive+Sampler+Spike
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-harness/pull/842
- Validator report example: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folder/validator-samples-2026-02

Risks and mitigation:
- Increased CI/GPU cost for strict validation: mitigate by using fecund sampling (downsample smartly) and enabling strict mode only for enterprise/on-demand builds.
- Overfitting to telemetry exports: include curated adversarial buckets and synthetic perturbations to avoid blind spots.

Next steps (owner: Liam O'Connor):
- Finish validator report template and implement auto-triage labels (this week).
- Add three additional adversarial buckets from security team (blocker: security review required).
- Schedule design review with PM and Console teams for the UI toggle (2026-03-17).
